IDS alerts were triggered but not escalated in time. Containment actions include blocking C2 infrastructure, revoking user credentials, and initiating endpoint remediation.

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Pattern {
    meta:
        description = "Detects memory patterns associated with Cobalt Strike beacons"
        author = "SOC_Team"
        severity = "critical"
    strings:
        $a = { 60 8B ?? 24 7C 8B 7C 24 1C 8B ?? 24 3C 8B 6C 24 } // Common beacon parsing routine
        $b = "Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 8.0;" wide ascii // Default user-agent
        $c = "x64" wide ascii
    condition:
        all of them
}

arguments.summary: Initial low-severity port scan alert escalated to critical incident following correlation with historical IDS alerts, EDR telemetry, and SIEM analysis. The source IP 10.0.5.14 was misidentified in initial monitoring; further investigation revealed the true compromised host was 10.0.5.42 (WS-FIN-042), a high-criticality finance workstation. Host exhibited Cobalt Strike beaconing (T1071.001), encoded PowerShell (T1566.001), lateral movement via SMB (T1021.002), and evidence of credential brute-forcing. A malicious PowerShell script downloading a remote payload was analyzed (T1105, T1059.001). Despite detection, containment actions (firewall block, EPP isolation) were denied due to procedural or targeting errors, indicating a critical gap in response automation and asset mapping.

EDR and SIEM correlation identifies true source as 10.0.5.42 (WS-FIN-042) with multiple TTPs.
Code analysis confirms malicious PowerShell script with remote payload download and code injection.
Containment actions (firewall block, EPP isolation) attempted but denied due to targeting and approval failures.
